work.permit: Approval of the Secretary (Employment Relations Act 2012, section 30(2))

note: Majority: not read; the Cook Islands' legislation is on PacLII (refused, Cloudflare) and its mirror (connections dropped); null. Work: Employment Relations Act 2012 (No. 17 of 2012), as the Ministry of Internal Affairs publishes it (a scan, read by eye), section 30: (1) an employer must not employ a person under thirteen; (2) an employer must not, without the approval of the Secretary, employ a school-age person during normal school hours, for more than ten hours a week outside them, or for work other than light work; (3) the Secretary approves only if the employment raises no educational or occupational safety and health risk; (5) a school-age person is one of at least thirteen and under sixteen (unless the Head of the Ministry of Education has let them leave school), and light work is work that doesn't threaten the child's health and safety or hinder education or training. So the general age is 16. Performers: a performer of thirteen to fifteen needs the Secretary's approval for anything beyond light work outside school hours (my reading: the Act names no performing rule of its own), and under thirteen is barred, so permit from 13. Service: the ILO's Child Labour Observatory profile says defence is New Zealand's responsibility; no law on a call-up was read; null.

An employer must not, without the approval of the Secretary, employ a school-age person— (a) during normal school hours; or (b) for more than 10 hours per week outside normal school hours; or (c) for work other than light work. ... aged less than 16 years
